# Hidden Cargo Tray Organizer

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Cut base first to cover angled tray area before turning over for stenciling after sanding tops. [t935]

## Tools

- [Partial] Butter knife [t935]

## Parts

- Attic insulation foam: Sold in 4'x8'x1.5" sheets [t935]

## Tips & gotchas

- Cut the base piece first to cover as much surface area of the angled tray as possible. [t935]
- Turn the base over before stenciling because the angled contours make it hard to see where lines are with foam in place. [t935]
- Sand the tops of both pieces after cutting and placing them, then stencil. [t935]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Cutting angles on all four sides without enough sanding can prevent the top piece from sitting flush so the lid closes properly. [t935]
